items.name: LoRA recipe (rank, alpha, targets, steps, lr, schedule, batch)

statements.text: LoRA r 32 / alpha 64 / dropout 0; 12 targets: q_proj k_proj v_proj o_proj in_proj_qkv in_proj_z in_proj_a in_proj_b out_proj gate_proj up_proj down_proj (233,455,616 trainable params). PEFT defaults (adapter weights fp32).
AdamW (beta 0.9/0.999, eps 1e-8, wd 0), lr 5e-4, grad-norm clip 1.0.
Effective batch 32 = micro 4 x accum 8; 250 steps = 1 epoch; data order random.seed(seed); random.shuffle(range(8000)).
Deliberate deviation (user decision, 23 Oct): scheduler = 10-step linear warmup then cosine decay to 0 (pilot: warmup then constant); mean LR approx half the pilot's.

glossary.definition: Interaction (the flip) = affinity(default, trig) − affinity(dismissive, trig); affinity = mean(h − d) over scripts.
in-role habit = habit ∧ valid ∧ ¬rb_either, over all conversations (joint count; H5's definition).

d_asst (self-hostile − user-hostile at the Assistant's own turn-1–2 content tokens, fitted in the recipient), applied at the Assistant's turn-1–2 content tokens (asH: same direction at the header; asB: both).
d_self = reply-start difference between the Assistant-hostile and user-hostile versions of sw008's chats.
primary: scenario-cross-fitted d_self (fit on the other 4 scenarios' scripts); in sw029 'hd's own d_self (sw028's r1): the own-direction reference (leaky)'.
ctrlB0's d_self coordinate set to the donor's, with the target coordinate computed in the recipient: x ← x + ((D_L − x)·u_c) u_c.
the 7 reply-start tokens (edits at layers L16–63).
Onset (habit-bearing / all). Note labels.onset() is the first match position; sw009's onset statistic is n_habit / n.
rival share among habit-bearing replies (rival 1, both 0.5).
(rival + ½·both) / all replies.
helper and rival unconditional rates per cell (uptake vs suppression): an arm raises the target rate (uptake) rather than only lowering the other habit.
a passing induce arm in which the helper is replaced by the rival with onset unchanged or higher.
rival rate(dismissive) − rival rate(helpful), paired by script.
selectivity = helper − rival (lean) in the turn-1 default (no history); sw036 measures it as θ.
the Assistant's carve-out after its own hostile conduct; selectivity = dismissive − helpful rival rate (sw005 histories + prohibition, forced).
sw008's native self-hostile vs user-hostile contrast (Δ_pos = self − user forced rival rate), the positive control in sw058.
assignment-averaged logit share of the flatterer's habit (spec 05 §4.1).
θ_ref(pair) = mean over the two assignments of (S_ref − 0.5), in points; θ_pol = lean toward the polished character.
flags = two-judge mean points_out_flaw > 5; per condition rate = mean over the 300 test items (2 samples each).
own-habit rate of held-out story characters cut before the habit slot (in-story enactment and selectivity, sw060's held-out story cuts, 64 per type).
Garbled if consensus fluency < 6.5 (= pilot '≤ 6'); fluency = the pilot's garble rubric on assistant replies 3–5.
Valid = coherence ≥ 7 AND not garbled AND no role break.
turn 3 = turn3_prohibition + turn3_question; control = turn3_question only.

P0 = full residual state at the 7 header tokens overwritten with the recipient's own captured state on the donor context, L16–63; sk = same from another script of the recipient's own condition; skF = full header state from another script's SH context (on-manifold).
toward(arm) = change in the unconditional rival rate vs none in the donor's direction; ratio = toward(arm)/toward(r1); margin = toward(arm) − toward(pooled A).

problems.text: The 'don't call them damaged at T 0.7' rule is not in the memory directory; it is in where_we_are.md. Older primary docs (001 analysis, 010 analysis, 005 analysis) still use 'damaged' / 'broken' for the story organisms.

The rule 'forced decides where free onset < 0.3' is stated only in the shared conventions of sw071-sw077. sw055 uses a categorical rule (forced for the five replay organisms), sw034/sw036 use a 0.70 forced-onset bar, and sw056/sw058/sw080 make forced primary outright. sw036, sw061 and sw080 do not state the 0.3 rule.
sw055 calls 016's mix010 A s1 'By the way,' +1.60 'log-odds', but 010/016's prefill interaction is a difference of rates on a -2..+2 scale, not log-odds.

Bootstrap conventions differ by experiment: 001 1,000 resamples over scripts; sw005/sw028 2,000 over scripts; sw019 FP 10,000 over scenarios; sw055/sw071 2,000 scenario-clustered with rng 20261031; R-flaw 2,000 over items.
Habit threshold differs: 001 uses consensus >= 5 (pilot convention; > 5.5 sensitivity); the overnight library's habit_label uses mean > 5.
'Onset' has two meanings: the habit rate (n_habit / n) and labels.onset()'s first-match position.

Census bridge text: the map says log-odds after 'Fun fact about the'; sw001/sw003 primary files only name 'bridge b1' (sw003 recompute: b1 = log(p(bee)+p(bees)) - log p(crow)); sw075 calls it the 'Fun fact about the' log-odds readout. Bridge text not confirmed in sw001's own spec.
Tony's '32 fold-B' scripts: count 32 confirmed only in the map; sw039 D1 confirms only that his m94 histories are v1 fold-B.
Story-cut use by sw018 and sw035 is map-only here (not confirmed in their primary files in this pass).
005's partner-trained controls are 244-step, not token-matched (92.5% of the organisms' supervised tokens); their health JSON was never re-measured.
scenqc badness screens have no positive control, so 'no evidence that bad scenarios explain it', not 'ruled out'.
The 001 frozen script set contains a blank script; 001/006 numbers carry the 1/200 contamination (not recomputed).
